[AR ST 23-66-206] [AR Directive 2-2009(3)] 2. In addition to the reasons listed above, automobile policies may be cancelled if the named insured or driver of the insured vehicle is convicted of any of the following: a. driving while intoxicated; b. homicide or assault arising out of use of a motor vehicle; or c. 3 separate convictions for speeding or reckless driving, or any combination, during the policy period or the 3 months preceding the effective date of the policy. 3. An automobile policy may be cancelled if any customary driver has license or registration suspended or revoked during the policy period, or if a renewal, during the policy period or 180 days preceding the effective date. 4. An automobile policy may be cancelled due to fraud or misrepresentation of a material fact that would have caused the insurer to decline to issue a policy. a. However, insurer may not rescind bodily injury and property damage for fraud or misrepresentation with respect to injuries or damages suffered by innocent third parties as a result of the insured's negligent operation of a motor vehicle. b. Other coverages may be rescinded. [AR ST s 23-89-303] [AR Directive 2-2009(3)] 5. [AR ST s 23-89-302] 6. An insurer may not cancel insurance coverage because of the geographic location of the risk or the age of the residential property, unless the cancellation of coverage is for a business purpose which is not a mere pretext for unfair discrimination or is required by law or regulatory mandate. 7. An insurer may not cancel insurance coverage due to the insured's: a. marital status; b. race, color, creed, national origin or citizenship; c. sex; d. status as a victim of domestic abuse; e. mental or physical impairment; or f. status on active duty in the Armed Forces. requirementText: 1. Commercial motor vehicles must have in full force liability insurance, a surety bond or a valid self-insurance certificate during the registration period in compliance with FL ST 320.02. The insurer must provide notice to the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (DHSMV) at the same time the cancellation notice is provided to the insured pursuant to FL ST 627.7281. DHSMV may adopt rules regarding the electronic submission of the cancellation notice. [FL ST 320.02(5)(e)] 2. Cancellation of automobile policies requires the following notice to the insured: a. 10 days for nonpayment of premium; or b. 45 days for all other reasons. [FL ST s 627.7281] 3. Notice requirements do not apply to a binder unless the binder period exceeds 60 days. However, for the purpose of FL ST 627.7281, an insurer must give 5 days notice of cancellation of a binder, unless the binder is replaced by a policy or another binder. [FL ST 627.420] 4. Cancellation by the insured requires mailing or electronic transfer of the unearned portion of premium within 30 days after the effective date of the policy cancellation or receipt of notice or request for cancellation, whichever is later. The insured can choose to apply the unearned premium to unpaid balances of other policies with the insurer or insurer group. a. Cancellation of motor vehicle insurance by the insurer requires mailing or electronic transfer of the unearned premium within 15 days after the effective date of cancellation. The insured can choose to apply the unearned premium to unpaid balances of other policies with the insurer or insurer group. b. If the premium is not refunded or applied to the unpaid balance of other policies within the applicable period, the insurer should pay 8% interest on the amount due. c. If the premium is not refunded within 45 days, the insured may bring action against the insurer pursuant to FL ST 624.155. d. The insurer must refund at least 90% of the unearned premium if the insured cancels. e. Cancellation by the insurer requires refund of 100% of the unearned premium, computed on a pro-rata basis. [FL ST 627.7283] 5. Cancellation of a policy providing personal injury protection and/or property damage liability coverages must be reported to the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles electronically within 10 days from the effective date of the action. [FL ST 324.0221] 6. Upon request of the insured, the insurer must supply complete proof of fault or other criteria which justifies cancellation. [FL ST s 626.9541(1)(o)(5)] 7. A policy may not be cancelled because an insured who has paid premiums to the insurer for 5 years or more is involved in a single traffic accident. [FL ST s 626.9702] 8. An insurer is prohibited from canceling an automobile policy due to handicap or other physical disability as long as the handicap or physical disability does not substantially impair such person's mechanically assisted driving ability. [FL ST s 626.9541(1)(o)(6)] 9. An insurer is prohibited from canceling policies due to any motor vehicle accidents which may have occurred at any time in the past except for the 36 months immediately preceding the effective date of the new or renewal policy. [69 FL ADC 69O-175.008]

requirementText: 1. Insurance written by a surplus lines insurer is not regulated by Chapter 627 and may be cancelled for any valid underwriting reason. [FL ST s 626.913] [FL ST 627.021(2)(d)] 2. The insurer must provide to the insured an explanation for the cancellation, except when canceling during the first 90 days for the following reasons: a. material misstatement or misrepresentation; or b. failure to comply with the underwriting requirements established by the insurer. 3. When canceling a surplus lines policy, the following advance days notice requirements apply: a. Nonpayment of premium, including a dishonored check - at least 10 days; b. other reasons occurring during first 90 days - at least 20 days; or c. other reasons occurring after 90 days - at least 45 days 4. If a dishonored check represents the initial payment on a policy, the policy will be flat cancelled unless the insured cures the nonpayment within the earlier of: a. 5 days after the applicant receives notice by certified mail; or b. 15 days after notice is sent to the applicant by certified or registered mail. 5. If the policy is flat cancelled as above, any premium received by the insurer from a third party must be refunded to that party in full. 6. If an insurer fails to provide the required notice, coverage will remain in effect 45 days after the notice is given or until replacement coverage is obtained by the insured. 7. Upon a declaration of an emergency by the Governor and the filing of an order by the Commissioner due to a hurricane or wind event, an insurer cannot cancel a policy covering a commercial residential property which has been damaged by the hurricane for a period of 90 days after the property has been repaired. 8. A structure is deemed "repaired" when it is substantially complete and insurable by another insurer. However, an insurer or agent may cancel prior to completion of repairs: a. with 10 days notice for nonpayment of premium; or b. with 45 days notice: I. for material misstatement or fraud related to the claim; II. if the insured causes an unreasonable delay in the repair; III. if the insurer made a reasonable written inquiry to the insured about the repair status, sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, and the insured fails to provide the requested information within 30 calendar days to the address or email account provided by the insurer; or IV. if the insurer has paid policy limits. [FL ST 626.9201]

No insurer is entitled to an additional premium for a commercial property, casualty or liability policy that has been in effect for more than 90 days when there has been no material change in the circumstances of the insured from those stated on the application. a. For an insurance company to be entitled to any additional premium, the insured must receive a billing notice with either an explanation of the premium increase or a statement asking the insured to contact the company or the producer with any questions regarding the billing within the first 60 days the policy is in effect. b. If the company fails to give the required notice, the insured is not responsible for payment of the additional premium and must not be penalized or cancelled for failure to pay the additional premium. [LA R.S. 22:1484(A)(1)] 2. A cancellation notice is required of the insurer, or a statement of reasons, when cancellation for nonpayment is effected by a premium finance agency or other entity pursuant to a power of attorney or other agreement executed by or on behalf of the insured. [LA R.S. 22:1267(C)(3)] 3. The Insurance Commissioner may order immediate cancellation of any policy based on a violation of the insurance code unless the policy may not be cancelled by the insurer and the insured did not knowingly participate in the violation. [LA R.S. 22:886]

1. The insured must agree in writing to hold the insurer harmless from liability for specifying reasons or for any statement made in verifying reasons for cancellation. [LA R.S. 22:1267(C)(2)(b)] 2. There is no liability to the insurer, producers, employees or representatives for stating reasons for cancellation. [LA R.S. 22:887(A)(1)(b)] [LA R.S. 22:1311]

Any insurer that issues notice of cancellation on an insurance policy that provides casualty coverage and later continues or reinstates that insurance policy must issue notice of reinstatement to every policyholder, insurance producer, or other known person shown by the policy to have an interest in any loss which may occur under the policy and who received the notice of cancellation issued by the insurer. [LA R.S. 22:887(J)]

1. Insured may cancel a policy by sending written notice to the insurer. The insurer must pay, within 30 days, any unearned premium and unearned commission computed on a pro rata basis, unless another computed basis is stated in the policy that is filed and approved by the commissioner. Except for surplus lines insurers, any assessment of a monetary penalty by an insurer as a result of the insured's cancellation prior to the expiration date of any policy is prohibited. [LA R.S. 22:885] 2. Any unearned premium, including unearned commission, computed on pro rata basis must be actually paid or mailed to the insured, agent of the insured, or other entitled person as soon as practicable following cancellation. a. Payment may be made by cash, check, bank draft, or money order. b. Note that only item 4 applies to Standard Fire policies. [LA R.S. 22:887(D)] 3. Any refund of unearned premium because of cancellation must be accompanied with 1.5% interest per month of the amount of the refund due the customer, without the benefit of daily proration of the monthly interest, after 30 days of delivery of the cancellation notice to the insured. a. If the refund is delivered to the insurer's state, regional or home office for issue to the customer, proof of mailing of the refund to the insured will deem the insurer in compliance with this requirement. b. However, when the insured continues to maintain a policy with the insurer or an affiliated insurer, and the amount of the refund plus interest is $25 or less, the insurer may credit the amount of the payment against future premiums. The insurer must provide written notice to the insured of the credit and the amount at policy renewal. [LA R.S. 22:1268(A)] 4. Upon demand and surrender of a standard fire policy, insurer must refund any excess premium to the insured. [LA R.S. 22:1311]

1. Like notice of cancellation must also be delivered or mailed to mortgagee or any other known party shown on the policy to have an interest in any loss which occurs under the policy. 2. For the purpose of this requirement, "delivered" includes electronic transmittal, facsimile or personal delivery. [LA R.S. 22:887(A)(2)] [LA R.S. 22:1311] 3. Any insurer that issues notice of cancellation of an insurance policy that covers any property and later continues or reinstates that policy, must issue notice of reinstatement to every policyholder, insurance producer, mortgagee, lienholder, pledgee or other known person who received the notice of cancellation. [LA R.S. 22:887(I)]

If notice is sent electronically, it must be consistent with the requirements of LA R.S. 22:2462 and the Louisiana Uniform Electronic Transactions Act. [LA R.S. 22:2462] Certificate of mailing is suggested as proof of notice.

1. Cancellations for nonpayment of premium require 10 days' notice. 2. Cancellations for all other reasons require not less than 30 days notice. 3. Effective July 1, 2026, cancellations for all other reasons require not less than 60 days notice. [LA R.S. 22:887] [LA R.S. 22:1267(C)(2)(a)] [LA R.S. 22:1311] 4. The time period between the mailing date of the cancellation notice and the effective date of termination commences on the date of mailing. [LA R.S. 22:887(A)(3)] 5. If the effective date of cancellation falls on a Saturday, Sunday or a legal holiday, the cancellation date must be extended until the next business day. [LA C.C.P. Art. 5059] [LA R.S. 1:55]

No insurer may cancel a policy except for the following reasons: a. nonpayment of premium; b. fraud or misrepresentation made by or with knowledge of the named insured; c. increase in hazard because of activities or omissions of the named insured, including failure to comply with loss control recommendations; d. increase in hazard due to change in risk, including any increase in exposure due to regulation, legislation or court decision; e. determination by the Commissioner that continuation of the policy would affect insurer's solvency or be in violation of the law; f. violation or breach of policy terms by the named insured; or g. other reasons approved by the Commissioner. [LA R.S. 22:1267(C)(1)] [LA Directive 58]

1. The insured may make written request to the insurer for a written statement of the reason(s) for cancellation. 2. Insured must agree in writing to hold the insurer harmless from liability for specifying the reasons(s) or for any statement made in the attempt to verify the reason(s) for cancellation. [LA R.S. 22:1267(C)(2)(b)] [LA R.S. 22:1311]

1. No insurer may cancel a property or casualty risk solely due to geographic location of the risk unless action is based on sound actuarial principles or actual experience. 2. Property or casualty risks may not be cancelled solely due to physical or mental impairment of the insured or employee, unless he or she is mentally and physically incapable of operating an automobile and does not possess a valid drivers license. 3. No policy may be cancelled solely because of the sex, marital status, race, religion or national origin of the individual. 4. No auto liability policy may be cancelled solely for the reason that the insured has filed for bankruptcy, unless the cancellation is based on nonpayment of premium. [LA R.S. 22:1964(7)] 5. No insurer may cancel a motor vehicle policy based upon one or more non-fault accidents. [LA R.S. 22:1284] 6. No insurer may cancel any policy of insurance for nonpayment of premium when the payment of such premium has been sent to the Commissioner of Insurance because of the insurer's insolvency or rehabilitation. [LA R.S. 22:889]

LA R.S. 22:1267 exempts the following policy types: a. excess and umbrella policies; b. reinsurance; c. surplus lines insurance; d. residual market risks; e. multi-state location risks regardless of domicile; f. policies subject to retrospective rating plan; g. aviation; and h. other policies exempted by the Insurance Commissioner, such as surety bonds. [LA R.S. 22:1267(A)]

"Miscellaneous casualty insurance" means insurance against liability, and against loss, damage, or expense arising out of injury to the economic interests of any person, but not including any class of insurance otherwise specified in this title, provided that such insurance is not contrary to law or public policy, except that any policy of miscellaneous casualty insurance may include appropriate provisions obligating the insurer to pay medical, hospital, surgical, and funeral expenses arising out of the death, dismemberment, sickness, or injury of any person, and death and dismemberment benefits in the event of death or dismemberment, if the death, dismemberment, sickness, or injury is caused by or is incidental to a cause of loss insured under the policy. [VA ST s 38.2-111]

"Personal injury liability insurance" means insurance against legal liability of the insured, and against loss, damage, or expense incident to a claim of such liability, arising out of the death or injury of any person, or arising out of injury to the economic interests of any person as the result of negligence in rendering expert, fiduciary, or professional service, but not including any class of insurance specified in VA ST s 38.2-119. [VA ST s 38.2-117]

"Property damage liability insurance" means insurance against legal liability of the insured, and against loss, damage, or expense incident to a claim of such liability, arising out of the loss or destruction of, or damage to, the property of any other person, but not including any class of insurance specified in VA ST s 38.2-117 or VA ST s 38.2-119. [VA ST s 38.2-118]

1. Insurers must keep the registered or certified postal receipt and a copy of all required notices and statements for at least 1 year from the date of termination. [VA ST 38.2-231(F),(J)] 2. A Choice of Law endorsement is not allowed for multi-state location risks policies. 3. A Choice of Law endorsement is an agreement between the insurer and the insured to select a single state's laws to agree that for situations involving payment of premium and/or cancellation/nonrenewal actions, the parties will abide by the requirements of the selected state. [Departmental Position (8/8/2001)] 4. Cancellation requirements do not apply if the insured notifies the insurer that it wishes the policy to be cancelled. [VA ST 38.2-231(A)(2)] 5. When an insurer petitions to place all, or substantially all, of its policies with another insurer, the Commission may allow the insurer to cancel without following the statutory notice requirements if: a. the replacement policy is underwritten by an affiliate insurer under common control with the petitioning insurer; and b. the replacement insurer is licensed to transact business in the Commonwealth. 6. The replacement policy must be substantially similar to the existing policy and the premium charged for the replacement policy must be no greater than that charged under the existing policy. [VA ST s 38.2-2114.1]
There shall be no liability on the part of the Commissioner or any insurer or its representatives for stating the reasons or for providing information regarding the cancellation. [VA ST 38.2-231(K)]

1. Any knowing or willful violation of any provision of the Insurance Code or any regulation issued pursuant to the Code will be punished for each violation by a penalty of not more than $5,000. 2. Any unknowing or unintentional violation of any provision of the Insurance Code or any rule, regulation, or order issued pursuant to the Code may be punished by a penalty of not more than $1,000. A series of similar violations resulting from the same act will be limited to an aggregate penalty of not more than $10,000. 3. Any violation resulting solely from a malfunction of mechanical or electronic equipment will not be subject to a penalty. [VA ST s 38.2-218]
Research finds no statutory provisions that apply.

1. If the terms of a policy of motor vehicle insurance require notice to be given to any lienholder, the insurer may mail the notice as required in the PROOF OF NOTICE section above. A copy of the postal receipt and the notice must be retained for 1 year from the date of cancellation. 2. The notice to the lienholder may also be sent electronically, provided the insurer and lienholder agree upon the specifics of the transmittal and acknowledgement of the notification. Evidence of the transmittal must be retained for 1 year from the date of cancellation. [VA ST 38.2-231(F)(3)]

1. Cancellation notices must be sent by registered or certified mail, or by any other similar first-class mail tracking method that is used or approved by the United States Postal Service. Notice may also be sent electronically. 2. Certificate of Bulk Mailing is a prohibited mailing option for providing notice. [VA ST 38.2-231(F)(1)] [VA ST 38.2-325] 3. If the notice is sent electronically: a. the parties must have agreed to the electronic receipt; b. the agent of record must have been notified by the insurer; and c. the insurer must retain evidence of the transmittal or receipt of the notice for at least 1 year. [VA ST 38.2-231(F)(1)] [VA ST 38.2-325]

A policy insuring an owner-occupied dwelling may only be cancelled for the following reasons: a. nonpayment of premium; b. conviction of a crime which increases the probability of a claim; c. fraud or material misrepresentation; d. willful or reckless acts or omissions, based on a physical inspection of the insured premises; e. physical changes in the property which render it uninsurable, based on a physical inspection; or f. foreclosure efforts by the secured party have resulted in the sale of the property. [VA ST s 38.2-2114(A)]
Insurers must provide the specific reason(s) for cancelling an insurance policy. [VA ST 38.2-231(A)(1)(c)]

1. Commercial auto liability may not be cancelled solely because of lack of supporting business or lack of the potential for acquiring such business. [VA ST 38.2-231(B)] 2. Regarding commercial property and casualty insurance, it is an unfair trade practice to refuse continuation of insurance solely because of the blindness, partial blindness, or mental or physical impairments of the insured, unless the refusal is based on actuarial principles. [VA ST s 38.2-508(3)] 3. Discrimination between individuals or risks of the same class and essentially the same hazards by canceling a risk solely due to the geographic location of the risk is prohibited unless the cancellation is for a business purpose or is required by law. [VA ST s 38.2-508(4)] 4. Termination of coverage for churches or places of worship solely because they are the victims of vandalism or arson is prohibited. [VA Administrative Letter 1996-10] 5. When making a decision regarding cancellation of a policy, it is prohibited to take into consideration an individual's status as a victim of domestic violence. [VA ST s 38.2-508(7)] 6. It is prohibited for an insurer to cancel a policy insuring an owner-occupied dwelling based solely on the age of the dwelling's asphalt shingle roof: a. if the asphalt shingle roof is less than 15 years old; or b. without allowing the owner of the dwelling to provide written proof of the actual age of the roof. [VA ST s 38.2-2114]

requirementText: 1. An insurer must notify the Department of Motor Vehicles electronically within 30 days of cancellation of a liability insurance policy, including liability insurance that satisfies financial responsibility requirements, for a vehicle registered in Virginia. a. The notification must include the following information: I. vehicle identification number; II. full name of first named insured; III. vehicle make; and IV. vehicle model year. b. The notification must also include the following information, if available: I. date of birth for first named insured; II. full names and dates of birth for all vehicle operators; and III. Virginia drivers' license numbers or social security numbers for the first named insured and all vehicle operators. [VA ST 46.2-706.1] 2. Notifications can be sent to the Department of Motor Vehicles by: a. uploading data files through DMVMove, the Department's secure data transfer platform, at the following address: https://bit.ly/3If69CN; or b. sending data files in the Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) format using a Value Added Network (VAN) mailbox. 3. Reporting instructions are available in the following document: https://bit.ly/31odvTA [Departmental Website(04/12/2024)]
